data.title: Procure to Pay workflows
data.lede: From need to payment: goods, services, returns, consigned stock and employee expenses, with the accrual, inventory and cost effect of each step.

scenarios.label: Goods: requisition to payment
scenarios.lede: Ingredients and packaging: from a planned or requested need to a reconciled payment. Inventory items accrue at receipt; the receipt, the delivery, the invoice and the payment each create accounting.

steps.title: Requisition
steps.description: Planning Central releases planned buy orders as requisitions; employees raise catalogue or non-catalogue requests. Approval runs by amount and category.
in: Planned buy order or employee request

steps.title: Purchase order
steps.description: The buyer (or automatic document creation) turns approved requisition lines into PO lines, priced from agreements. The approved PO schedule becomes an expected receipt.
out: Approved PO, communicated to the supplier

steps.title: Supplier ships
steps.description: The supplier ships the goods. An advance shipment notice (ASN) from the Supplier Portal or EDI lets Receiving receive against it.

steps.title: Receive and inspect
steps.description: Goods are received against the PO schedule or ASN and inspected for food safety. Lot numbers and expiry dates are captured at receipt.

impacts.text: inventory purchases accrue at receipt: the uninvoiced receipt is a liability from this point

steps.title: Receipt accrual
steps.description: Receipt Accounting books the receipt into inspection against the uninvoiced receipts accrual.

steps.title: Put away to stock
steps.description: Delivery moves the lots from receiving into the ingredient or packaging subinventory. On-hand increases by lot and expiry date.

impacts.text: on-hand quantity increases by lot, with its expiry date

steps.title: Inventory valuation
steps.description: Cost Accounting values the delivery. Under standard cost (US plant) the difference between PO price and standard cost is purchase price variance.

impacts.text: PPV = (PO price − standard cost) × quantity under standard cost

steps.title: Supplier invoices
steps.description: The supplier sends the invoice for the PO.

steps.title: Import and match
steps.description: The invoice is imported (AP_INVOICES_INTERFACE) or keyed, then matched to the PO (2-way) or to the receipt (3-way).
process: Match to purchase order or receipt

steps.title: Validate and approve
steps.description: Validation checks matching tolerances and places holds; it calculates tax and price variances. The approval workflow routes the invoice; Create Accounting books it.

impacts.text: the invoice relieves the uninvoiced receipts accrual
invoice price variance when the invoice price differs from the PO

steps.title: Match receipt accruals
steps.description: Receipt Accounting pairs the invoice with the receipt accrual; Clear Receipt Accrual Balances clears what remains by rule.

impacts.text: accrual balance cleared; residuals cleared by rule

steps.title: Pay
steps.description: A payment process request selects due installments, builds and formats payments and transmits the file (see Treasury › Payments to bank). FBCo accounts payments at issue and at clearing.

steps.title: Bank pays supplier
steps.description: The bank executes the payments and reports them on the statement.

steps.title: Reconcile
steps.description: The statement line is matched to the payment. Reconciliation clears the payment, which accounts the move from cash clearing to cash.

notes.title: Accrual policy.
notes.text: Inventory purchases must accrue at receipt; expense purchases may accrue at period end (see Services and expense items).

notes.title: Mexico.
notes.text: FBCo México uses perpetual average cost: the receipt updates the item's average cost instead of creating a purchase price variance.

notes.title: Two US business units.
notes.text: US Manufacturing BU is the Procurement Services BU for US Distribution BU: DC requisitions become POs there, supplier sites are assigned to both US invoicing BUs, and the DC's receipts and invoices are accounted in company 102.

scenarios.label: Services and expense items
scenarios.lede: MRO, maintenance and professional services: amount-based or expense lines that never enter inventory. They can be matched to a work confirmation or receipt, or paid on 2-way match, and accrue at period end.

steps.title: Requisition
steps.sub: fixed price service or expense item
steps.description: A requester orders a service (Fixed Price Services line type: category, description, total amount) or a non-stock item charged to an expense account.

steps.title: Purchase order
steps.description: The PO line carries the amount and the expense charge account. Fixed price services are received and matched by amount.

steps.title: Service performed
steps.description: The supplier performs the service and may submit a work confirmation in the Supplier Portal.

steps.title: Receive by amount
steps.description: The requester confirms delivery by amount (or quantity for expense items). No inventory is created.

steps.title: Period-end accrual
steps.description: Received but uninvoiced expense lines are accrued at period end and reversed in the next period.

impacts.text: accrued at period end, reversed next period

steps.title: Supplier invoices
steps.description: The supplier invoices the service.

steps.title: Match and validate
steps.description: The invoice is matched to the PO (2-way) or to the receipt; validation checks tolerances. Without an accrual, the invoice books the expense directly.

steps.title: Pay
steps.description: Paid in the same payment run as goods invoices (see Treasury).

notes.title: Two policies.
notes.text: Accrue at receipt credits the accrual when goods arrive; accrue at period end credits Payables when the invoice is processed, and Receipt Accounting accrues uninvoiced receipts at period end.

scenarios.label: Supplier return
scenarios.lede: A lot fails inspection or is damaged: it goes back to the supplier, the PO reopens for the returned quantity and a debit memo reduces what FBCo owes.

steps.title: Inspection fails
steps.description: The lot is rejected in inspection, or found damaged after delivery. A return needs a valid receipt and a PO that isn't canceled or final closed.

steps.title: Return to supplier
steps.sub: Return to Receiving + Return to Supplier
steps.description: Receiving creates a Return to Receiving and a Return to Supplier transaction and reopens the PO for the returned quantity. Lot numbers are entered on the return.

impacts.text: on hand reduced when the return is from stock (lot entered)

steps.title: Goods back to supplier
steps.description: The supplier takes the goods back and issues a credit, or replaces them.

steps.title: Reverse receipt accounting
steps.description: The return reverses the receipt accrual (and inventory valuation if delivered).

steps.title: Debit memo
steps.description: Depending on the supplier site setting, a debit memo is created automatically for the return; otherwise Payables creates it manually. It isn't automatic for consigned items.
process: Create debit memo from the return

cr: Uninvoiced receipts accrual (or the original charge)

steps.title: Net in next payment
steps.description: The negative debit memo is selected with the supplier's other due invoices in the next payment run.

notes.title: Credit vs replacement.
notes.text: If the supplier replaces the goods instead of issuing credit, the PO reopened by the return is received again and no debit memo is needed.

scenarios.label: Supplier-consigned inventory
scenarios.lede: Packaging held at the plant but owned by the supplier until FBCo uses it. Consumption transfers ownership; a periodic consumption advice is the basis for the invoice.

steps.title: Consignment agreement
steps.description: A consignment agreement with the supplier sets the price used when stock is consumed.

steps.title: Supplier ships
steps.description: The supplier ships against a consignment order.

steps.title: Receive as consigned
steps.description: Received goods are held as consigned stock: in FBCo's possession, owned by the supplier. They are accounted in consigned clearing and accrual accounts, not owned inventory.

impacts.text: on hand increases, owning party = supplier

steps.title: Consume
steps.description: Using the stock (for example a material issue) triggers consumption under the consumption rules: a Transfer to Owned transaction, then the movement itself.

impacts.text: ownership moves to FBCo at consumption

steps.title: Value owned stock
steps.description: The transfer to owned is priced from the consignment agreement at the consumption date; the consigned entries reverse and a normal owned receipt follows.

impacts.text: liability to the supplier recognised at consumption

steps.title: Consumption advice
steps.description: Create Consumption Advice summarises consumption for the supplier (by supplier and site) and sends it by print, email or the Supplier Portal. It is the document for financial settlement.

steps.title: Invoice matched to advice
steps.description: The supplier invoice is matched one-to-one to the consumption advice; with Pay on Use on the agreement, Create Consumption Advice creates a self-billed invoice.

scenarios.label: Employee expenses
scenarios.lede: Travel and plant-visit expenses: corporate card transactions and cash expenses on an expense report, approved, audited and reimbursed through Payables.

steps.title: Card transactions file
steps.description: The corporate card issuer sends transaction files; Upload Corporate Card Transactions loads and validates them, and valid transactions become expense items.

steps.title: Expense report
steps.description: The employee picks card transactions and adds cash expenses, marking card items business or personal, then submits.

steps.title: Approve and audit
steps.description: The manager approves; the auditor then checks receipts and policy on Audit Expense Report (complete, reject, request information, short pay, adjust accounting). Status becomes Ready for payment processing.

steps.title: Create the invoice
steps.description: Process Expense Reimbursements and Cash Advances fills the Payables open interface and runs Import Payables Invoices, creating employee (and card issuer) payment requests.
process: Process Expense Reimbursements and Cash Advances

steps.title: Reimburse
steps.description: The employee is paid by the payment run (electronic or check).

notes.title: Payment options.
notes.text: Individual Pay: the employee pays the card issuer. Company Pay: FBCo pays the issuer for all transactions. Both Pay: FBCo pays business items and the employee pays personal ones.

data.title: Make and inventory workflows
data.lede: Production, co-packing, transfers, counts, lot control and costing for the plants and the distribution centre.

scenarios.label: Plan to produce
scenarios.lede: Process manufacturing: plan, release and run a work order from the recipe (work definition), then cost it through work in process to finished-good lots and variances.

steps.title: Run plan
steps.description: Forecasts and sales orders are netted against on-hand and open supply; planned make orders are recommended.

steps.title: Release planned order
steps.description: The planner releases planned make orders; Supply Chain Orchestration receives them as supply requests.

steps.title: Supply request
steps.description: Orchestration creates the work order and tracks it, raising exceptions when supply changes.

steps.title: Process work order
steps.description: The work order copies the recipe: ingredients in, primary output and co-products out. Work orders from other systems come in through the open interface.

steps.title: Issue ingredients
steps.description: Ingredient lots are issued to the work order, pushed or backflushed; backflush can default lots first-expiry, first-out.

steps.title: Ingredient lots out
steps.description: On-hand ingredient lots fall as they are issued.

steps.title: Resources and overhead
steps.description: Resource transactions charge labour and machine hours; overhead absorption rules add overhead.

impacts.text: WIP charged with resources and overhead

steps.title: Complete product
steps.description: Finished-good and co-product lots are completed with expiry dates into the completion subinventory.

steps.title: Finished goods on hand
steps.description: Completed lots are on hand and available to Order Management.

steps.title: Cost the work order
steps.description: Cost Accounting values issues, resources and completions; Create Accounting sends them to the ledgers.

impacts.text: standard cost (US) or perpetual average cost (MX)

steps.title: Close work order
steps.description: The work order is closed once production is complete.

steps.title: Variances
steps.description: The remaining WIP balance goes to usage and efficiency variances; gross margins can then be analysed by product.

notes.title: Costing methods.
notes.text: Cost Management supports standard, actual and perpetual average cost. The mock company uses standard cost in the two US cost organisations (plant and distribution centre) and perpetual average cost in Mexico.

scenarios.label: Co-packer (outside processing)
scenarios.lede: A step of the recipe, for example bottling or packing, is done by a co-packer as a supplier operation on the process work order. FBCo keeps ownership of the goods throughout.

steps.title: Work order with supplier operation
steps.description: The work order includes a supplier operation. Outside processing is supported for both discrete and process manufacturing.
in: Work definition with a supplier operation

steps.title: Supply order
steps.description: On release (or prior operation completion, per plant parameter) Manufacturing asks Orchestration to create a purchase requisition.

steps.title: OSP purchase order
steps.description: Self Service Procurement creates the requisition; Purchasing creates the outside processing PO from the blanket agreement for the OSP service item.

steps.title: Complete prior operation
steps.description: Quantities are reported complete at the operation before the supplier operation.

steps.title: Ship to the co-packer
steps.description: Orchestration creates an Outside Processing shipment line; the shipment is confirmed and closed, printing packing slip and bill of lading.

steps.title: Co-packer processes
steps.description: The co-packer performs the operation and returns the goods, with an ASN where needed.

steps.title: Receive into the work order
steps.description: Receiving receives and delivers to the work order; for nonserialized operations the supplier operation is completed automatically.

steps.title: Continue the work order
steps.description: Production continues with the next operation; quantities can be completed, scrapped or rejected, and returned to the supplier.

steps.title: OSP cost to WIP
steps.description: Receipt Accounting accounts for the receipt of the OSP item; Cost Accounting charges WIP when it is delivered to Manufacturing (purchase cost for average or actual, standard cost for standard items).

impacts.text: receipt accrual, as for any receipt
OSP service cost included in WIP

steps.title: Co-packer invoice
steps.description: The co-packer invoices the service; it is matched to the OSP PO and receipt like any PO invoice.

notes.title: Full outsourcing.
notes.text: Oracle's contract manufacturing flow (the whole product made by a contract manufacturer against a sales order) is supported only for discrete manufacturing, so a process manufacturer outsources steps as supplier operations.

scenarios.label: Plant to DC transfer
scenarios.lede: Finished goods move from the US plant (US Manufacturing BU, company 101) to the US distribution centre (US Distribution BU, company 102) on a transfer order. The two are profit centres of one legal entity, so an intracompany financial orchestration flow prices the transfer and Cost Accounting books both sides; no invoices are raised.

steps.title: Transfer request
steps.description: Transfer requests come from planning, min-max, requisition lines, spreadsheets or the supply order service; Orchestration decides transfer order or PO.

steps.title: Transfer order
steps.description: The transfer order represents demand and supply in one document, to an inventory or expense destination.

steps.title: Intracompany flow
steps.description: The transfer crosses profit centre business units in the same legal entity, so an intracompany financial orchestration flow applies. The transfer price comes from the transfer pricing rules for the financial route (here cost-based, at the plant's standard cost; a markup is possible).

steps.title: Pick, pack, ship
steps.description: Shipping picks and ships the lots; with the in-transit transfer type the goods are in transit until received.

impacts.text: plant on hand reduced; quantity in transit

steps.title: Trade distributions
steps.sub: plant cost org · DC cost org
steps.description: Cost Management costs the shipment in the plant cost organisation and creates trade distributions for the receivable and payable between the two business units: an intracompany trade may not need an invoice. Intercompany balancing adds no lines because the entry already balances by company.

steps.title: Receive at the DC
steps.description: The DC receives against the transfer order using the receipt routing set for in-transit transfers, then puts away.

steps.title: DC inventory value
steps.description: The receipt moves value from in transit into the DC cost organisation at the transfer price.

notes.title: Two cost organisations.
notes.text: Inventory organisations in one cost organisation must belong to the same profit centre business unit, so the plant and the DC are valued by separate cost organisations (both standard cost).

notes.title: Within one legal entity.
notes.text: The intracompany receivable and payable sit in companies 101 and 102 of the same ledger; they net to zero for FBCo US and need no consolidation elimination. Account names are INFERRED.

notes.title: Mexico to US.
notes.text: A transfer between FBCo México and FBCo US crosses legal entities: Financial Orchestration prices it and raises intercompany invoices (see Order to Cash › Intercompany sale).

scenarios.label: Cycle count and physical inventory
scenarios.lede: Ingredients and packaging are cycle counted by ABC class; a full physical inventory runs at year end. Approved differences adjust on-hand and are expensed.

steps.title: Cycle count definition
steps.description: Counts are defined by ABC class or category, with count frequency and approval tolerances; A items are counted more often than B items.

steps.title: Schedules and sequences
steps.sub: Generate Count Schedules · Generate Count Sequences
steps.description: The scheduled processes pick the items due and create one count sequence per item, lot, subinventory and locator with on hand; a listing report prints them.

steps.title: Record and approve
steps.sub: Record Count Sequences · Approve Count Sequences
steps.description: Counters record quantities; differences beyond tolerance go for approval. Sequences with reservations can't be approved.

impacts.text: on hand adjusted to the count

steps.title: Physical inventory
steps.description: Transactions stop; a snapshot freezes on-hand quantities (no reservations should exist).

steps.title: Tags and counts
steps.description: Tags are generated and printed; counters record them (dynamic or blank tags for stock found).

steps.title: Approve and post
steps.description: Adjustments are approved, rejected or reset, then posted as material transactions against the adjustment account.

impacts.text: on hand adjusted to the count

steps.title: Cost the adjustments
steps.description: Count adjustments are miscellaneous transactions: a shortage credits inventory valuation against the offset (adjustment) account.

scenarios.label: Lot expiry, holds and recall
scenarios.lede: Food safety: lots are held by material status, expired lots are actioned and scrapped, and a recall traces lots by genealogy and contains them.

steps.title: Inspect at receipt
steps.description: Receipts are inspected; lots can be graded (for example excellent, average, poor) for quality control.

steps.title: Material status hold
steps.description: Material statuses restrict what can be done with a lot, for example blocking shipment of chilled goods after a refrigeration failure. Quality inspection action rules can change the status automatically.
process: Quality action rule: Change Material Status

impacts.text: lot not available to issue or ship

steps.title: Lot expires
steps.description: Lots of shelf-life items carry an expiry date; the expiration action (from the item, the lot or the transaction) says what to do when it expires.

steps.title: Scrap
steps.description: The expired or rejected lot is issued to a scrap account. Expired lots can't be reserved but can still be transacted, so scrapping is a deliberate step.

steps.title: Scrap cost
steps.description: The scrap is valued and expensed to the offset account on the transaction.

steps.title: Recall notice
steps.description: A supplier letter or regulator notice recalls an ingredient FBCo received; Product Recall Management captures it as a recall notice and resolves duplicates.

steps.title: Locate recalled parts
steps.description: Locate Recalled Parts traces the recalled lots across on hand, in transit and open purchase orders.

steps.title: Count, quarantine, dispose
steps.description: Tasks: Perform Physical Count and Quarantine Recalled Parts, then Perform Scrap or Return to Supplier. The notice line closes when its tasks are done.
process: Perform Physical Count and Quarantine Recalled Parts
Perform Scrap or Return to Supplier for Recalled Parts

steps.title: Debit memo to supplier
steps.description: A debit memo recovers the cost of recalled parts from the supplier.
process: Raise Debit Memo Against Disposition for Recalled Parts

notes.title: Customer recalls.
notes.text: Oracle Product Recall Management handles inbound recalls (parts FBCo received). A recall of FBCo's own products from customers runs outside it: lot genealogy, customer returns (Order to Cash › Customer return) and credit memos.

scenarios.label: Standard cost update
scenarios.lede: Once a year (and for new items) the US cost organisations (plant and distribution centre) set new standard costs in a cost scenario, rolls them up through the recipes and publishes them; on-hand and open work orders are revalued.

steps.title: New costs
steps.description: Ingredient and packaging standards, resource and overhead rates are loaded or entered.

steps.title: Cost scenario
steps.description: A cost scenario holds the new standard costs, resource rates and overhead rates, effective from a date. State: New.

steps.title: Roll up costs
steps.description: Rollup builds finished-good costs from the work definitions: ingredients, resources, overhead and any outside processing cost. State: Costs Rolled Up.

steps.title: Publish
steps.description: Publishing makes the costs effective on the scenario date (state Costs Published). Undo Cost Update works only before the costs are used.

steps.title: Revalue on hand and WIP
steps.description: On hand is revalued by (new − current standard) × quantity; open work orders get a WIP standard cost adjustment.

impacts.text: new standards drive future PPV and variances

notes.title: Mexico.
notes.text: FBCo México uses perpetual average cost, so it has no standard cost update; its costs move with each receipt, and the Create Cost Adjustments page corrects them when needed.

data.title: Order to Cash workflows
data.lede: From customer order to cash in the bank, plus returns, drop shipments and the intercompany sale from Mexico.

scenarios.label: Standard order to cash
scenarios.lede: A retail order by EDI: credit-checked, scheduled and reserved, picked first-expiry first-out, shipped, invoiced, recognised, paid by lockbox and reconciled. In the US the order, shipment and invoice belong to US Distribution BU (company 102), which owns the distribution centre.

steps.title: Customer PO
steps.description: Retail purchase orders arrive by EDI; smaller customers use a portal.

steps.title: Sales order
steps.description: The order is imported through DOO_ORDER_HEADERS_ALL_INT or the Sales Orders for Order Hub REST API; an orchestration process runs each fulfilment line.

steps.title: Credit check
steps.description: Credit check runs first, then approval. A failing order goes to Credit Review Pending; Receivables Credit Management opens a credit case folder and the analyst releases the hold or raises the limit.

steps.title: Schedule and reserve
steps.description: Global Order Promising schedules the line and reserves supply until shipment.

steps.title: Pick, pack, ship
steps.description: Lots are picked first-expiry, first-out, packed and ship-confirmed; ship confirm issues inventory (Direct Sales Order Issue).

steps.title: Deferred COGS
steps.description: The sales order issue is costed into deferred COGS until revenue is recognised.

steps.title: Invoice
steps.description: Create Billing Lines sends the line to RA_INTERFACE_LINES_ALL; Import AutoInvoice creates the invoice with tax (US sales tax, MX VAT).

steps.title: Recognise revenue
steps.description: Deferred revenue is recognised when its contingencies are met.

steps.title: Recognise COGS
steps.description: Cost Accounting moves deferred COGS to COGS in proportion to recognised revenue; ship-only lines can use the order-line close date.

steps.title: Customer pays
steps.description: The customer pays to FBCo's lockbox; the bank sends the lockbox file.

steps.title: Lockbox receipt
steps.description: Process Receipts Through Lockbox imports the file into AR_PAYMENTS_INTERFACE_ALL, validates it and posts the receipts; Apply Receipts Using AutoMatch applies what is left.

steps.title: Reconcile
steps.description: The statement line is matched to the receipt by reconciliation rules.

scenarios.label: Customer return
scenarios.lede: A retailer returns a damaged pallet: a return order (RMA), receipt back into the warehouse, a credit memo and the cost reversal.

steps.title: Customer returns
steps.description: The customer asks to return goods from a fulfilled or closed order line.

steps.title: Return order (RMA)
steps.sub: Return for Credit and Return Item
steps.description: The return references the original line (returnable quantity = ordered minus prior returns) and sets the warehouse that receives it. Return for Credit gives credit without the goods.

steps.title: Receive the return
steps.description: The warehouse receives against the RMA and puts the goods away (or into a quarantine subinventory).

steps.title: Receipt confirmation
steps.description: The scheduled process imports the receiving status into Order Management.

steps.title: Credit memo
steps.description: Billing sends the return line to AutoInvoice, which creates a credit memo (the transaction type is Credit Memo for return lines).

steps.title: Cost of the return
steps.description: The return receipt is costed back into inventory, reversing COGS.

notes.title: Damaged goods.
notes.text: Returned lots that can't be resold are put away to a quarantine subinventory and scrapped (see Make & Inventory › Lot expiry, holds and recall).

scenarios.label: Drop ship
scenarios.lede: A food-service customer orders an item FBCo doesn't stock: the supplier ships straight to the customer and FBCo bills it.

steps.title: Sales order
steps.description: The supplier ships the order directly to the customer, bypassing FBCo's plants and warehouses.

steps.title: Requisition and PO
steps.description: Supply Chain Orchestration creates a purchase requisition for each drop ship line; Purchasing turns it into a drop ship PO.

steps.title: Supplier ships to customer
steps.description: The supplier ships and either sends an ASN or just invoices FBCo.

steps.title: Customer receives
steps.description: The goods arrive at the customer's site.

steps.title: Drop ship receipt
steps.sub: ASN option or AP invoice option
steps.description: The ASN, or the AP invoice, generates a drop ship receipt and delivery, which starts costing and billing.
process: Transfer Invoice Details to Supply Chain Financial Flow Orchestration
Transfer Ownership Change Events to Receiving

impacts.text: costed as a receipt and an immediate sales issue; no on-hand change

steps.title: Supplier invoice
steps.sub: matched to the drop ship PO
steps.description: Payables matches the supplier's invoice to the PO.

steps.title: Bill the customer
steps.description: The shipment record releases billing; AutoInvoice creates the customer invoice.

notes.title: Returns.
notes.text: A drop shipment can't be returned straight to the supplier: it comes back into a warehouse first, then goes to the supplier.

scenarios.label: Intercompany sale MX → US
scenarios.lede: The Mexican plant ships concentrates to the US distribution centre. The goods move once; Financial Orchestration creates the intercompany sale in Mexico and the purchase in the US at a transfer price. The buyer is US Distribution BU (company 102).

steps.title: Transfer request
steps.description: Planning or min-max at the US DC requests supply from the MX plant.

steps.title: Ship from MX
steps.description: The MX plant ships the lots; the physical shipment starts the financial flow.

steps.title: Financial orchestration
steps.description: Processes the shipment event and prices it with the transfer pricing rules (cost plus a markup).

steps.title: Intercompany AR invoice
steps.description: Mexico invoices the US entity at the transfer price.

steps.title: Intercompany AP invoice
steps.description: The US entity records the payable.

steps.title: Receive at the US DC
steps.description: The DC receives and puts the lots away.

impacts.text: US on hand increases at transfer price

steps.title: Cost both sides
steps.description: Mexico relieves inventory to intercompany COGS; the US values the receipt at the transfer price.

notes.title: Eliminations.
notes.text: Intercompany revenue, COGS and the margin left in US inventory are eliminated in consolidation (Record to Report › Consolidation).

data.title: Record to Report workflows
data.lede: The month-end sequence to the balance sheet and P&L, then each GL process in detail: boundary journals, intercompany, allocations, FX, consolidation and reconciliation.

scenarios.label: Month-end sequence
scenarios.lede: The order the close runs in, from opening the period to reporting the balance sheet and P&L. Each bubble has its own scenario tab where there is more to show.

steps.title: Open the period
steps.description: The accounting period is opened in each ledger (and reporting currency) before journals are created or imported; MXN/USD daily rates are loaded.

steps.title: Close subledgers in order
steps.description: Supply chain closes first (inventory and receipt accounting), then Payables, Receivables, Cash Management and Assets. See Period close for the day-by-day calendar.

steps.title: Create Accounting
steps.description: Each subledger's Create Accounting applies the accounting method and transfers journals to GL; for Mexico it writes primary and secondary journals together.

steps.title: Payroll and treasury journals
steps.description: The external payroll provider and treasury send journal files (see Boundary journals).

steps.title: Import and post journals
steps.description: Feeder and spreadsheet journals come through GL_INTERFACE; journals are approved and posted.

steps.title: Intercompany
steps.description: Intercompany balancing adds due-to and due-from lines between FBCo US and FBCo México, and balances journals across companies 101 and 102 inside the US ledger through the clearing company; intercompany allocations and transactions are completed (see Intercompany).

steps.title: Allocations
steps.description: Plant overhead and shared services are allocated (see Allocations).

steps.title: Revalue
steps.description: Foreign-currency balances are revalued at the period-end rate (see FX).

steps.title: Secondary and reporting
steps.description: The MX secondary ledger and the USD reporting currency are complete once the primary ledger's journals and revaluation post.
process: Review the secondary ledger and reporting currency

steps.title: Translate
steps.description: Balance-level translation where a translated view is needed.

steps.title: Close the periods
steps.description: The ledgers' periods are closed.

steps.title: Load FCCS
steps.description: GL balances are loaded into FCCS (see Consolidation).

steps.title: Consolidate
steps.description: FCCS translates and eliminates intercompany and produces consolidated results.

steps.title: Reconcile accounts
steps.description: Balance-sheet reconciliations are prepared and reviewed (see Account reconciliation).

steps.title: Report BS and P&L
steps.description: Consolidated statements from FCCS; ledger-level statements from Financial Reporting on the USD ledger set, and by company (101, 102, 201) for each business unit. Data access sets by primary balancing segment value let each US business unit's accountants work on their own company.

scenarios.label: Boundary journals
scenarios.lede: Journals from outside Oracle: the external payroll provider, and treasury (deals and bank interest). They arrive as files in the Journal Import format.

steps.title: Payroll journal file
steps.description: The payroll provider sends summarised journals per pay run (HCM is out of scope).

steps.title: Treasury journals
steps.description: Treasury sends journals for deals and interest not created in Cash Management.

steps.title: Load to GL_INTERFACE
steps.description: The file is uploaded to UCM and loaded into GL_INTERFACE, by hand or through the ERP Integrations REST resource (importBulkData).

steps.title: Import Journals
steps.description: Import Journals validates and creates the journal batches.

steps.title: Approve and post
steps.description: Journals are approved and posted.

notes.title: Bank fees and interest.
notes.text: Fees and interest that appear on the bank statement are created in Cash Management as external transactions and accounted there (see Treasury › Bank statement to reconciliation).

scenarios.label: Intercompany
scenarios.lede: Charges between FBCo US and FBCo México that are not trade (for example management fees): an intercompany transaction, invoices or journals in both entities, and reconciliation.

steps.title: Enter transaction
steps.description: The provider enters an intercompany batch with a transaction type; batches are numbered automatically or manually.

steps.title: Receiver approves
steps.description: The receiver is notified and approves the transaction.

steps.title: Provider invoice
steps.description: Where the transaction type requires invoicing, it is transferred to Receivables (memo line per transaction type).

steps.title: Receiver invoice
steps.description: The matching payable is created in the receiver.

steps.title: Or journals only
steps.description: Types that don't need invoices are transferred to GL as journals; intercompany balancing rules add the due-to and due-from lines.
process: Transfer Intercompany Transactions to General Ledger

steps.title: Reconcile
steps.description: Intercompany receivables and payables are agreed between the two ledgers before close.

steps.title: Eliminate
steps.description: FCCS eliminates the intercompany balances through plug accounts.

notes.title: Within FBCo US.
notes.text: Charges between US Manufacturing BU (101) and US Distribution BU (102) are journals in one ledger. The same balancing rules apply; set the clearing company option (use the clearing company for intracompany journals) so many-to-many journals don't error. No invoices and no consolidation elimination are needed.

notes.title: Rule levels.
notes.text: Balancing rules are defined by primary balancing segment value, legal entity, ledger or chart of accounts, in that order of precedence.

scenarios.label: Allocations
scenarios.lede: Plant overhead spread to product lines by production volume, and shared services (procurement and finance in US Manufacturing BU) spread by headcount: to US Distribution BU within the US ledger, and to FBCo México across legal entities.

steps.title: Allocation rule
steps.description: Rules define the pool, the basis and the target accounts.

steps.title: Generate allocations
steps.description: Calculates the allocation and, if Post Allocations is selected, books it through Journal Import. An allocation from company 101 to 102 stays in the US ledger: balancing adds the intracompany lines through the clearing company.

steps.title: Cross-entity allocations
steps.description: Allocations across legal entities create intercompany transactions: one batch per provider, one transaction per receiver.

steps.title: Post
steps.description: Allocation journals post to the ledger.

scenarios.label: FX: revaluation and translation
scenarios.lede: Mexico buys some ingredients in USD and the US holds MXN intercompany balances: revaluation at period end, reporting currency conversion and translation.

steps.title: Daily and period rates
steps.description: Rates are loaded daily and at period end.

steps.title: Revalue Balances
steps.description: Foreign-currency balances (USD payables in Mexico, MXN intercompany in the US) are revalued; the result is unrealised gain or loss.

steps.title: Reporting currency
steps.description: MX journals are converted to USD as they post into the reporting currency.

steps.title: Translate
steps.description: Balances are translated at period-end and average rates; equity uses historical rates; the difference goes to the cumulative translation adjustment.

scenarios.label: Consolidation in FCCS
scenarios.lede: GL trial balances go to FCCS through Data Integration; FCCS consolidates from local currency through translation to eliminations.

steps.title: Closed trial balances
steps.description: Final balances after the ledger close.

steps.title: Source and mappings
steps.description: The ERP connection and the GL application are registered; segments map to FCCS dimensions and members.

steps.title: Run integration
steps.description: The integration extracts the GL balances and loads them into FCCS, with filters and adjustment periods.

steps.title: Local currency
steps.description: Opening balances carry forward; movements are calculated; the balance sheet is balanced; local-currency rules run.

steps.title: Translate
steps.description: Entity data is translated to the parent currency; differences go to the CTA account.

steps.title: Eliminate and consolidate
steps.description: Intercompany balances are eliminated through plug accounts, and configurable consolidation rules run.

steps.title: Reports
steps.description: Consolidated balance sheet and P&L.

scenarios.label: Account reconciliation (ARCS)
scenarios.lede: Reconciliation Compliance runs a six-step process each period for balance-sheet accounts.

steps.title: Balances
steps.description: GL and subsystem balances are available.

steps.title: Load data
steps.description: Balances load from a file or through Data Integration or Data Management.

steps.title: Auto reconcile
steps.description: Reconciliations for zero-balance accounts, or where source and subsystem balances match, complete automatically.

steps.title: Notify and prepare
steps.description: Preparers are notified and justify the balance with reconciling items, explanations and attachments.

steps.title: Review
steps.description: Reviewers approve, monthly, quarterly or when risk conditions are detected.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.description: Dashboards show progress and late work.

data.title: Treasury workflows
data.lede: Payments out to the bank and bank statements back in, reconciled in Cash Management.

scenarios.label: Payments to bank
scenarios.lede: The weekly supplier payment run: installments selected, validated and reviewed, payments built and formatted, the file transmitted to the bank with a positive pay file, then cleared from the statement.

steps.title: Select installments
steps.description: A payment process request (or template) selects validated, approved installments by due date, pay group and currency.

steps.title: Review and validate
steps.description: Stages: installment selection, document validation, payment validation; proposed payments can be reviewed and approved.

steps.title: Build and format
steps.description: Payments assigns the bank account and payment process profile, creates payments and the payment file, then extracts and formats it.

steps.title: Transmit
steps.description: The file is transmitted to the bank (or checks are printed); payments are confirmed at formatting or transmission.

steps.title: Positive pay
steps.description: A positive pay file of issued checks goes to the bank to block fraud.

steps.title: Bank pays
steps.description: The bank pays suppliers and reports the debits on the statement.

steps.title: Reconcile and clear
steps.description: Reconciliation matches the statement lines to the payments and clears them (event class Reconciled Payments: Payment Cleared).

impacts.text: cash credited when the bank pays

notes.title: Accounting option.
notes.text: FBCo accounts payments at issue and at clearing: issue credits cash clearing; clearing moves cash clearing to cash. That keeps cash equal to the bank.

scenarios.label: Bank statement to reconciliation
scenarios.lede: Each morning the banks' statements load, reconcile automatically to receipts, payments and journals, and bank fees and interest are created and accounted in Cash Management.

steps.title: Statement file
steps.description: The bank publishes the previous-day statement (and intraday statements).

steps.title: Load and import
steps.description: The scheduled process retrieves the file and loads and imports it; a manual route loads a file from UCM with Load and Import Bank Statement, and spreadsheets use the FBDI template.
process: Import Bank Statements from a Spreadsheet

steps.title: Autoreconciliation
steps.description: Matching and tolerance rules match statement lines to payments, receipts, journals and external transactions.

steps.title: Exceptions and manual
steps.description: Ambiguous, date and amount exceptions are reviewed; manual reconciliation handles 1:1, 1:M, M:1 and M:M matches.

steps.title: Fees and interest
steps.description: Transaction creation rules turn unreconciled first-notice lines (bank charges, fees, interest) into external transactions, which are then reconciled.

steps.title: Create Accounting
steps.description: Reconciled external transactions are accounted with their cash and offset accounts and transferred to GL.

impacts.text: ledger cash agrees with the bank

notes.title: Transfers between accounts.
notes.text: Manage Bank Account Transfers creates an outflow and an inflow external transaction, accounted by Create Accounting.

notes.title: Interface tables.
notes.text: The spreadsheet route loads CE_STATEMENT_HEADERS_INT, CE_STATEMENT_LINES_INT and related balance tables.

data.title: Assets workflows
data.lede: Capital purchases into assets, depreciation, the Mexican tax book and retirement.

scenarios.label: Capital purchase to asset
scenarios.lede: A new filling line: bought on a PO charged to asset clearing, invoiced, sent to Assets as a mass addition, capitalised and depreciated.

steps.title: Asset PO
steps.description: To send an asset purchase to Assets, the natural account on the PO charge account must be an asset clearing account.

steps.title: Asset invoice
steps.description: The supplier invoice is matched to the PO; its amount goes to asset clearing.

steps.title: Create Mass Additions
steps.description: Sends approved, accounted invoice lines charged to asset clearing (or CIP clearing) to Assets as mass additions (FA_MASS_ADDITIONS).

steps.title: Post Mass Additions
steps.description: Mass additions are reviewed (merged or split) and posted as assets.

steps.title: Calculate Depreciation
steps.description: Depreciation runs each period for the corporate book.

steps.title: Create Accounting
steps.description: Asset journals transfer to GL.

steps.title: Post
steps.description: Journals post in the corporate ledger.

notes.title: Receipt-based assets.
notes.text: Assets can also be created from receipts: estimated costs transfer from the receipt to the corporate book of the inventory organisation.

scenarios.label: Asset transfers, tax book and retirement
scenarios.lede: After capitalisation: transfers between cost centres, the Mexican tax book kept by mass copy, and retirement with sale proceeds and cost of removal.

steps.title: Transfer
steps.description: Transfers move the asset's assignment; the Transfers infotile shows old and new details.

steps.title: Perform Periodic Mass Copy
steps.description: Additions, adjustments, retirements and reinstatements copy from the corporate book to the tax book each period, without skipping periods; the tax book accounts to the MX secondary ledger.

steps.title: Retire
steps.sub: full or partial, cost or units
steps.description: The asset is retired, fully or partly, by cost or by units.

steps.title: Sale proceeds
steps.description: The buyer's payment is recorded against proceeds of sale clearing.

steps.title: Cost of removal
steps.description: The removal contractor's invoice is charged to cost of removal clearing.

steps.title: Gain or loss
steps.description: Gain or loss = proceeds − cost of removal − net book value retired + revaluation reserve retired. Calculate Gains and Losses runs between partial retirements in a period.

steps.title: Post
steps.description: Asset journals post to the ledgers.

data.title: How the ledgers relate
data.lede: FBCo US has one primary ledger. FBCo México has a primary ledger in MXN, a secondary ledger with the Mexican statutory chart, and a USD reporting currency. Select a ledger or a step to see how data reaches it.

nodes.title: Subledgers
nodes.subtitle: AP · AR · Cost · Receipt · Assets
nodes.description: Subledger transactions in both countries raise accounting events.
functions: Create Accounting applies the accounting method of each ledger
For Mexico one run creates primary and secondary journals (subledger level)

nodes.title: Asset books
nodes.subtitle: Corporate book · MX tax book
nodes.description: Fixed Assets keeps one corporate book per primary ledger. The MX tax book is assigned to the MX secondary ledger.
functions: Corporate book: Create Accounting for Assets → primary ledger
Tax book: Perform Periodic Mass Copy from the corporate book, then accounted to the secondary ledger
Payables asset invoices and the tax-book addition use the same conversion rate, so asset clearing clears in both ledgers

nodes.title: GL journals
nodes.subtitle: Manual · spreadsheet · GL_INTERFACE
nodes.description: Journals entered in GL or imported through GL_INTERFACE.
functions: Posting in the MX primary ledger copies them to the secondary ledger (journal conversion rules)
Posting also converts them to the USD reporting currency

nodes.title: US primary ledger
nodes.subtitle: USD · corporate COA · US GAAP
nodes.description: The main record of FBCo US.
functions: Corporate chart of accounts, accounting calendar, USD
Both US business units post here (company values 101 and 102)
Revalues MXN balances (for example intercompany payables) at month end

nodes.title: MX primary ledger
nodes.subtitle: MXN · corporate COA
nodes.description: The main record of FBCo México, kept in the local currency on the corporate chart so that group reporting is consistent.
functions: Corporate chart and corporate accounting policies
Source for the secondary ledger and the USD reporting currency
Revalues USD balances (for example supplier invoices in USD)

nodes.title: MX secondary ledger
nodes.subtitle: MXN · statutory COA
nodes.description: The Mexican statutory books, linked to the MX primary ledger.
functions: Data conversion level: Subledger
Different chart of accounts (Mexican statutory) through the chart of accounts mapping
Same currency as the primary (MXN), which avoids difficult reconciliations
IVA and retention entries reach the statutory chart in the same run (EB-Tax tab); MX statutory accountant only (Security tab)

nodes.title: MX reporting currency
nodes.subtitle: USD · corporate COA

notes.title: Cash basis in Oracle.
notes.text: Tax point basis Payment: invoice accounting debits (or credits) an interim tax account; payment or receipt accounting moves the paid share to the final account and reports it as of that date. Partial payments move a proportionate amount.

notes.title: Why withhold at payment.
notes.text: Mexican IVA and ISR retentions arise when the supplier is paid, so the calculation point is Payment and the tax authority invoice is created at payment.

notes.title: Not in scope.

notes.title: To verify.
notes.text: Renewal of the border-region 8% decree beyond 2025, and partial-payment behaviour when withholding at payment combines with cash-basis IVA (test in the test environment).

notes.title: One role, many scopes.
notes.text: Roles say what a user can do; data access says where. An AP specialist role is the same in the US Distribution BU and the MX BU, with different data access assignments. Avoid one role per BU.

notes.title: Role codes are illustrative.
notes.text: FBC_ codes show the naming convention, not a delivered catalogue; each is a copy of the matching Oracle job role, trimmed where an SoD rule requires it.
